Nexus Architecture Atlas
Present chapter: Nexus Architecture Atlas

This walkthrough maps Nexus's durable user flows to their owning components.

User flow	Primary owner	Supporting contract	Evidence
Install or repair media	scripts/installer/	Owner-aware lease and atomic runtime state	Installer tests plus packaged operator run
Generate an image	desktop/sidecar/src/diffusion/dispatcher.ts and Python pipelines	Shared diffusion readiness API	PNG validator and retained artifact
Edit or recover a saved image	desktop/sidecar/src/studio/imageEditRuntime.ts and the Image Studio viewer	Revisioned recipes, approval checkpoints and viewer recovery; shared originals retained	Approval, retry, restart, restore and revocation tests
Generate a video	desktop/sidecar/src/diffusion/videoDispatcher.ts and Python pipelines	Shared diffusion readiness API	Video probe and retained artifact
Browse and install models	core/registry/ and Settings	Shared availability/recommendation tuple	Cross-language rank fixture
Read chat usage	core/chat/ and shared chat UI	Role-local token provenance	Protocol, hydration, and UI tests
Organize chats and work across folders	Chat explorer, Coding page and workspace scope	Persisted folder colors; union-of-roots path boundary	Database reopen, picker, persistence and denial tests

End-to-end path
Present chapter: End-to-end path

Catalog-source reachability checks and desktop payload preparation are packaging prerequisites. The installer provisions the media runtime.

The sidecar reads the atomic readiness record and exposes one repair contract to Image Studio and Video Lab.

Generation jobs check the selected model directory layout before loading models and finalize artifacts before reporting success.

The desktop renders truthful capability, model, transcript, archive, and workspace state from shared contracts.

Packaged acceptance requires installing the exact candidate, retaining the installer-to-payload binding, and exercising the installed runtime with the media smoke harness. The harness alone does not establish that binding.

Release-specific logs and test counts live in the corresponding release or archive tree.

Generation Recovery and Validation
Present chapter: Generation Recovery and Validation

This handbook describes the supported operator path for recovering local image and video generation after an interrupted install. It applies to the packaged Windows installer and installed Nexus desktop application.

Saved Image Studio edits have a separate recovery path. Each agent approval attempt captures the complete saved edit and undo/redo history before access can be granted; a storage failure grants no access. In the image viewer, open "Recovery checkpoints", inspect the approval metadata, choose a checkpoint and confirm "Restore and save". Pending edits are saved first. Recovery replaces the current edit history, ends earlier agent access to that image and refuses a conflicting revision; reload if another editor changed it. Deleting an image session or folder removes its history, edits and checkpoints, while shared original image files stay on disk.

Recover the runtime
Present chapter: Recover the runtime

Close Nexus and any active installer window.

Rerun the exact NexusSetup.exe candidate to provision or recover the local runtime.

Let the installer reclaim only a lease whose owner is proven dead or mismatched. A live or uncertain owner remains protected.

Treat the install as successful only when the runtime readiness probe reaches ready. A selected media capability that remains unavailable is a required failure.

Validate image and video generation
Present chapter: Validate image and video generation

Install the exact candidate first and retain evidence that the installed payload came from it. Then run scripts/installer/build/smoke-installed-media.ps1 against that installer artifact and installed sidecar. The harness records the supplied installer hash and exercises the installed runtime; it does not install the candidate or establish that binding itself. Retain one decodable PNG and one playable video, runtime versions, model ids, elapsed time, artifact hashes, and probe metadata.

The PNG proof includes format, dimensions, non-zero pixel content, and SHA-256. The video proof includes codec, duration, frame count, dimensions, and SHA-256. Unit tests and mock CUDA runs do not replace this packaged evidence.

Interpret failures
Present chapter: Interpret failures

REPAIR_BUSY means a verified live owner holds the repair lease.

REPAIR_OWNER_UNKNOWN means ownership cannot be proved safely; stop the competing process or reboot before retrying.

runtime-unavailable means the installed media environment failed readiness. Repair is available when its required components are present; missing components require rerunning the installer. Generation remains unavailable until readiness succeeds.

A missing PNG or video after the exact packaged run blocks release publication.

See the installer runtime and media runtime companions for component ownership.

Installer Repair and Runtime State
Present chapter: Installer Repair and Runtime State

The installer owns dependency provisioning and repair. diffusion_venv_provisioner.py owns the versioned repair lease; runtime_provisioner.py atomically publishes the installer's runtime-readiness snapshot. runtimes/diffusion/repair.py records desktop repair attempts in the same runtime contract.

The lease identifies its process by PID plus process-start identity and attempt nonce. A stale record is reclaimed only after ownership is disproved. Desktop repair records a repairing attempt, publishes ready after its backend smoke succeeds, or records failed with a failure code. An interrupted attempt remains visible for recovery.

Hugging Face repository, revision, exact file path, and gated status are catalog data. Run the catalog reachability checker as a packaging qualification step; the Windows build script does not invoke it automatically. Public models never open an authorization dialog. Genuine gated models use explicit account, license, sign-in, device-code, copy, manual-token, and skip controls.

sections.text:
Local Media Runtime
Present chapter: Local Media Runtime

The desktop sidecar exposes one vendor-neutral readiness and repair API from desktop/sidecar/src/diffusion/runtimeFactory.ts. Image and video runtimes consume that API rather than deriving readiness independently from GPU telemetry or model presence.

Runtime readiness checks the interpreter and recorded backend smoke; generation preflight checks the selected model layout. Image execution produces PNG bytes, and video execution checks non-empty frames and finalizes an MP4 file after a file-size and container-header check. Full artifact decoding is part of packaged qualification. The bounded Repair action is available when the installed contract contains the required repair components; other failures retain their actual code and may require installer rerun or corrected input.

Packaged qualification is stronger than internal tests: the exact installed sidecar must produce a PNG with non-zero pixels and a video with valid codec, duration, frames, and dimensions.

Local Media Runtime

Transcript and Agents Workspace
Present chapter: Transcript and Agents Workspace

Chat usage is separated by message role. User bubbles show only the user message's input-token count. Assistant bubbles show visible reasoning plus visible answer tokens, while request and context input totals remain in Activity telemetry. Token provenance records whether counts are exact or estimated.

An empty pending response renders on the transcript canvas with a safe inset and no message bubble. A pending response that already has content retains its bubble. Completed metadata stays inside each bubble above content. Reasoning is collapsed above the answer by default, and ordinary message clicks do not open a duplicate preview panel.

Agents uses the installed recommendation snapshot before presenting a model selection. Workspace folders, Chat/Memory/Activity tabs, and collapsible session history share one main pane. The workspace scope authorizes the union of selected roots; operations outside every selected root remain denied.

Chat explorer folder colors are saved in the local chat database and survive application restart. Use a folder's context menu to change its color or clear it. A failed save shows an error and leaves the stored color unchanged. The shared explorer adapter refreshes from storage and discards tree responses that began before a successful mutation, so an older read cannot replace the current color. Folder colors do not change workspace permissions.

Document Output
Present chapter: Document Output

The experimental document_outline and document_read_section tools and their Settings controls have been retired following the owner's removal decision and the frozen evaluation fallback. They are absent from the extension, desktop, scheduled and ACP tool registries. This page retains its existing URL so older links still explain the outcome.

Document Parsing
Present chapter: Document Parsing

Generic OCR and parse_document remain available under their independent opt-in. In the desktop app, Settings > Security still offers "Enable parse_document for coding sessions". NEXUS_PARSE_DOCUMENT and nexus.coding.parseDocument.enabled retain their existing behavior. The removed outline settings and NEXUS_DOCUMENT_OUTLINE / NEXUS_DOCUMENT_OUTLINE_SUMMARIES environment variables cannot restore the retired tools.

parse_document reads up to 50 pages per call. Its extracted text is redacted, screened as untrusted content and sized against the active model's context window and the room left in the conversation. Use a smaller max_pages when output is truncated. This limit does not guarantee answer quality or increase the OCR runtime's own capabilities.

Conversation Space
Present chapter: Conversation Space

The output budget still uses backend prompt usage where available and a conservative fallback otherwise. It reserves room for the answer, applies a fixed-share ceiling and reports a nearly full window. The extension, desktop, scheduled runner and ACP preserve their active-model context lookup for document parsing.

Both agent loops retain tool-result compaction and native tool-history behavior. Native Ollama calls keep assistant tool calls and tool-role results. OpenAI-compatible paths and saved sessions retain their existing supported history representation; retirement does not claim to close their recorded native-history gaps.

Retained Evidence
Present chapter: Retained Evidence

The frozen expanded evaluation found cross-section accuracy below the promotion threshold: Qwen 3.5 9B scored 0/20 and Gemma 4 12B scored 4/20. The owner selected removal, so no repeat of the futile benchmark is authorized by this change. Historical plans, raw measurements, fixtures and reports remain evidence of that result; they do not describe an enabled current feature. See the evaluation record.

Existing ~/.nexus/outline-cache files and saved user preference keys are retained. Retirement neither reads those keys to enable tools nor deletes cached data. Restarting the app ends any old in-memory tool instances; the new composition cannot create outline tools. Standalone algorithm and historical fixture support may remain in source without a product registration.
